subject: Foundry Systems — Edge cluster ops & network segregation: architecture review
messages:
From: Kerry Lang <kerry.lang@foundrysys.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Edge site cluster ops — initial blueprint and ask

Hi Jonas / Irene,

Thanks again for taking a look. Attached are the draft rack-level diagrams and our current network segmentation workbook (files attached below). We're planning to host a pair of 3-node Kubernetes clusters at our Stockton facility: one for inference (GPU-enabled) and one for control/ingest (CPU-only). Key asks:

- Validate node pool sizing (we're considering 3x A100-equivalent for inference, 2x for burst)
- PV strategy: want encrypted block storage with fast local NVMe ephemeral for caches and an NFS-backed tier for logs/retention
- Network: strict tenant isolation between inference and customer workloads, and a separate management VLAN with limited egress
- Confirm required firewall/NAT rules for Redwood Private control-plane access and diagnostics over our site VPN

Our timeline: kickoff workshop next week (target Nov 4–6), followed by an on-site acceptance test in early December. Can you review the attached and call out any missing dependencies or non-starters from Redwood's side?

Attachments: (Attachment: foundry-edge-blueprint.pdf, application/pdf) (Attachment: network-segmentation-v2.xlsx, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Thanks — happy to hop on a call.

Kerry Lang
Head of Infrastructure
Foundry Systems
kerry.lang@foundrysys.com
+1 415-555-0123

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com>
To: Kerry Lang <kerry.lang@foundrysys.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood-inference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Edge site cluster ops — initial blueprint and ask

Kerry — thanks for the clear deck and the segmentation sheet. High-level feedback after a quick pass:

- Node pools: 3 inference GPUs for primary is reasonable; recommend we provision a 4th warm-standby or use burst capacity policy to avoid hot-fail scenarios. We'll propose a 3+1 layout in the runbook.
- Storage: agree with NVMe ephemerals for cache; for persistent volumes we prefer encrypted blockstore (LUKS) per PV with an additional NFS/backup target for long-term logs. We'll call out snapshot/retention SLAs in the runbook.
- Network: segregation looks good; we will require an out-of-band management VPN endpoint and a pair of IPsec tunnels for control-plane egress. Also recommend an internal transit firewall to enforce service egress (control plane, telemetry) and to prevent cross-tenant lateral movement.
- Diagnostics: we need a reachable diagnostics endpoint from Redwood (only over the IPsec tunnels) and a short list of allowed ports (SSH for jumpbox, 443 for control, 8123 for telemetry).

Action items before the workshop:
1) Kerry: can you confirm the rack PDUs and whether BMC access is available across all nodes?
2) Kerry: export of current VLAN IDs and a basic ACL snapshot into the Drive folder above.
3) Irene/Jordan: we'll prepare a short ops runbook draft (node pools, PV classes, CSI config, failure scenarios) and a proposed test plan for the acceptance window.

I'll schedule a 60-minute working session for Nov 5 10:00–11:00 PT unless that conflicts. If that works, Jordan can send a calendar invite.

- Jonas
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com
(Attachment referenced: network-segmentation-v2.xlsx)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood-inference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com>, Kerry Lang <kerry.lang@foundrysys.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Edge site cluster ops — initial blueprint and ask

Thanks team — quick technical notes to seed the runbook.

Prelim node-pool recommendation (to include in draft runbook):
- inference-pool (gpu): 3 x A100-40GB (primary) + 1 x A100-40GB warm standby; Taints: dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule; ResourceLimits: single-pod per GPU for predictable isolation.
- burst-pool (gpu-burst): 2 x A100-40GB (spot-like) with preemption handling hooks to replay requests to primary.
- control-pool (cpu): 3 x 32CPU/256GB nodes (kube-system, ingress, metrics, operator daemons).

Storage profile:
- csi-redwood-luks (type: block, encrypted): default for inference PVs; snapshot policy daily, retention 30 days.
- fast-ephemeral (local-nvme): emptyDir-backed caches with PodDisruptionBudget guidance.
- archive-nfs (nfs): long-term logs/metrics; mounted read-only for analytics cluster.

Network constraints and required firewall rules (draft):
- Allow outbound to control.redwood-inference.com:443, telemetry.redwood-inference.com:8123 from management VLAN only.
- Block east-west access between tenant subnets; allow egress to NVIDIA driver repositories and container registries.
- Management VPN: IPsec/DUO MFA; only agreed maintenance CIDRs permitted.

I'll attach a short YAML snippet in the runbook for the PV classes and CSI parameters. Jordan — if you can include the basic test checklist (node drain, PV failover, snapshot restore) that will complete the first draft.

Irene Choi
Principal SRE, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood-inference.com
(Attachment: runbook-seed.yml — to be added to Drive)

Jonas / Irene — really helpful, thanks. Nov 5 10:00 PT works for us — please send an invite.

Quick answers: PDUs will be redundant per rack, BMC access is available but needs to be routed over our management VLAN (credentials will be provided during the workshop under NDA). VLAN export and ACL snapshot uploaded to the Drive folder (see link). We'll also add a short compliance note on encryption-at-rest requirements for our auditors.

Next: we'll expect the draft runbook and the test checklist by COB Nov 3 so our infra team can prep for the acceptance. Also can you flag any contract changes needed to support warm-standby GPUs and on-site spares? That'll feed into procurement.

I'll wait for Jordan's calendar invite.

Thanks — Kerry
